positions.name: Oracle Corporation
positions.sector: Technology Services — Packaged Software (enterprise applications + Oracle Cloud Infrastructure / AI compute)
positions.catalyst: Oracle reported fiscal Q1 FY2027 after the close on 9/10 and it was a clean double beat with a forward number attached. Revenue $19.35B vs. ~$19.14B consensus, +~30% y/y. Adjusted EPS $1.92 vs. $1.74 consensus, a 10% beat. The line that matters is Oracle Cloud Infrastructure: OCI revenue MORE THAN DOUBLED, +121% y/y to $7.4B in the quarter ended 8/31, and total cloud revenue rose 62% to $11.6B. Remaining performance obligations stand at $638B. Critically — and this is the exact thing yesterday's AVAV pick did NOT have — management gave forward guidance rather than a reaffirm: 58-64% y/y cloud order growth. ORCL closed 9/10 DOWN 5.38% at $152.94 on 56.8M shares (2.0x its 28.5M average) into the print, spiked to $167.67 in the after-hours, faded to $158.30 overnight, and has spent the last three pre-market hours rebuilding and consolidating in a tight $162.12-$164.39 band on rising volume. Bid $163.50 / offered $163.82 as of 10:38:04Z.
positions.driver: ENTRY IS NOT A CHASE, AND THE ARITHMETIC IS THE WHOLE ARGUMENT. $163.62 is +7.0% over yesterday's close, inside the 8-10% ceiling. But yesterday's close was itself a 5.38% down day into the print on 2x volume. Measured against the 9/9 close of ~$161.63, this entry is +1.2%. We are paying roughly the pre-flush price for a company that has since printed 121% OCI growth and guided cloud orders up 58-64%. THE OVERNIGHT TAPE ALREADY STRESS-TESTED THE GAP. This is the part that separates ORCL today from CHYM, MU and AVAV before it. Those names were bought at the pre-market high with no evidence the gap could hold. ORCL's gap has already been round-tripped once and bought back: $167.67 high, $158.30 overnight low, then a steady rebuild to $163-164 across the 08:00-10:30Z pre-market window with volume climbing (217K, 82K, 79K, 49K, 83K on the last five half-hour bars). The weak hands have already sold and the price is back near the top of the range. We are buying a tested gap, not a fresh one. WHERE THE DOWNSIDE PROTECTION COMES FROM. ORCL trades at $163.62 against a 52-week high of $331.00 set on 9/11/2025 — it is 50.6% off its high, exactly one year to the day. The AI-capex de-rating in this name has already happened; there is no crowded momentum long left to unwind, which was the failure mode in every losing trade this book has taken. P/E is 27.7 on a $441B market cap for a business compounding revenue at 30% and cloud at 62% — not cheap, but not a multiple that requires perfection either. THE STOP IS TECHNICAL, NOT ARBITRARY. $152.54 sits below both yesterday's close ($152.94) and yesterday's session low ($152.61). To hit it, ORCL must fully retrace the entire earnings gap AND break the prior session's low on a day it beat revenue, beat EPS, doubled OCI and raised the cloud-order outlook. That is a genuine thesis invalidation, not noise. LIQUIDITY IS THE QUIET EDGE. 28.5M average daily volume on a 1.71B float, $441B cap. Unlike AVAV (1.8M ADV) or the small-cap gappers on the board, this stop will actually fill where it is placed — the position cannot gap through it on a thin book. RUNNERS-UP AND WHY THEY LOST. Kroger reported pre-market and is quoted $57.27 bid against a $56.95 close, i.e. +0.6% — a consumer bellwether with no asymmetry. American Eagle (-15%), Navan (-15.4%) and Cooper Companies (-17%) are the losers' list, not candidates. Energy is the direct beneficiary of Brent above $106 and record $6 diesel, but crude has now run seven sessions and buying it here is the definition of chasing the very move that is driving the CPI risk. Defense (yesterday's AVAV) has spent its catalyst. AVGO, MU and NVDA are all up 0.4-1.1% pre-market on sympathy with no fresh news of their own — they are the read-through, and ORCL is the source. ORCL is the only name on the board with a large, fresh, company-specific catalyst that has survived an overnight stress test and still has not been fully paid for.
positions.risks: (1) AUGUST CPI PRINTS AT 8:30AM ET TODAY, ~50 MINUTES AFTER ENTRY, AND THIS IS THE DOMINANT RISK IN THE TRADE. It is not hedgeable inside a 100% single-name long and it should not be minimized. Consensus is +3.4% y/y headline, unchanged from July; the Cleveland Fed nowcast is +0.36% headline / +0.2% core. Fed funds futures now put the odds of a 25bp HIKE next week at 72%, up from a coin flip a week ago, driven by Brent above $106 and diesel at a record $6/gal. A hot core print pushes those odds toward certainty, and the single most rate-sensitive cohort in the market is long-duration AI-capex equity — which is precisely what ORCL is. A 27.7x multiple on a capex-heavy cloud buildout is exactly what gets compressed when the discount rate moves against it. The offset is that ORCL's idiosyncratic catalyst is unusually large (121% OCI growth is not a macro number), and that it has already de-rated 50% from its high so it is not the crowded long the market unwinds first. But if CPI runs hot, this position will be down on the day regardless of the beat. That is the trade being taken. (2) FOUR-DAY LOSING STREAK — THE MARGINAL BUYER HAS BEEN ABSENT ALL WEEK. The three major indexes are on pace for a weekly decline and have closed lower four sessions running. Futures are only +0.3% this morning. In this tape, beats have not been paid for: AEO beat and fell 15%, NAVN beat and fell 15.4%, and yesterday's AVAV beat by 97% and still closed the rotation down. A gap-and-fade is the primary loss path and this book has lived it five times. The mitigation is structural — the overnight already tested and rebought the gap — but the pattern is live. (3) 'SELL THE NEWS' ON A STOCK THAT HAD ALREADY RUN. ORCL is up ~43% off its $114.50 July low. Some of the AI-cloud enthusiasm was pre-positioned into the print, which is arguably why it sold off 5.4% on 2x volume the day before rather than rallying into it. The after-hours $167.67 print that faded to $158.30 is evidence that supply exists above $165. (4) CAPEX AND MARGIN SCRUTINY IS THE STRUCTURAL BEAR CASE. OCI growth of 121% is being bought with enormous data-center capital expenditure, financed partly with debt, at gross margins below Oracle's legacy license business. The market has repeatedly punished this name when the conversation shifts from RPO growth to free cash flow and balance-sheet leverage. A single sell-side note today reframing the quarter around capex intensity or RPO concentration in a small number of customers could reverse the gap intraday. $638B of RPO is only as good as the counterparties behind it. (5) 24-HOUR HOLD SPANS A WEEKEND-ADJACENT FRIDAY WITH LIVE GEOPOLITICAL RISK. The rotation exits Monday 9/14 at 6:35am CT, so this position carries the full weekend: an active U.S.-Iran conflict, oil above $106, and the FOMC meeting on 9/15-16 immediately after the exit. Weekend headline risk in either direction is unhedged, and Monday's open can gap through the stop even in a liquid name. (6) ONE-YEAR ANNIVERSARY OF THE TOP IS A REAL TECHNICAL LEVEL, NOT A COINCIDENCE. The 52-week high of $331.00 was set 9/11/2025. Annual-lookback and momentum screens rebalance off that date, and the stock rolling off a -50% year can change how systematic funds classify it in either direction.
